# Selling part of a holding bought at a rate with three decimals.
#
# The basis is `fx_sell_part_of_a_lot_bought_at_a_three_decimal_rate.txt`:
# 100.00 USD at 1.405 CAD/USD, costing 140.50 CAD — a whole number of cents,
# so the basis is booked as stated and its cost per unit is the 1.405 that
# file wrote.
#
# 33.00 USD of it therefore cost 33 × 1.405 = 46.365 CAD. That is half a cent,
# which no split can hold, and money rounds away from zero: the book makes
# this sale worth 46.37. So 46.37 is the one figure this split may state, and
# the check that reads it rounds the same way before comparing.
#
# The sale fetched 46.00, so the residual is the 0.37 lost on it.
#
# {basis_guid} is filled in from `fx-balances`.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_a_sale_is_valued_at_its_basis.py.
2026-03-01 * "Sell 33 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD -33.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.405"
		value: "-46.37"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{basis_guid}"
	Assets:Bank 46.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "46.00"
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
